variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button): the first decision step, with empty memory and no execution steps, is always A. Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. Choose A, press button, only when the button_pressed value you write at THIS step is `no`: that is, the memory carried in says `no` or is empty AND no execution step shown here shows the press (neither the pressed-down label nor the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers). Every rule below likewise uses the button_pressed and pending_cubes values written at this step, not the carried ones. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes as written at this step (the list is ordered by the cubes' position in the observation listing at the button-press step, and the first entry is always the next cube to pick); never choose by distance from the gripper, by x or by y. Point at that stored [y, x], or at the cube visible within a few pixels of it (cube positions wobble). If no cube is currently listed at that position it is merely hidden by the arm: still choose B at the stored point; never switch to another entry for that reason and never treat the list as empty. 4. Only when the pending_cubes carried in was already empty, nothing was picked up at this step, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op. A step that merely shows a placing (fingers reopened, cube back on the table) with a non-empty carried list is not finished: apply rule 3 and choose B at the first entry of pending_cubes. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Write `no` when the memory carried in says `no` (or is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the press (neither the pressed-down label nor the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers). At the first decision step, when the memory carried in is empty, write the starting value `no` explicitly; never leave the field blank. Write `yes` as soon as any execution step shown at this step either says the button is pressed down, or shows the gripper within a few pixels of the button's [y, x] at a height of about 0.02-0.04 with fingers nearly closed (0-2% open); the highlighted areas then vanish from the listing before the decision step, which confirms the press. Either sign alone is enough; do not wait for the label. Write `yes` also whenever the memory carried in already says `yes`. Never go back to `no`. e.g. yes
fields.annotation: `no` at step #1 (nothing has happened yet), written explicitly, never left blank. `yes` at every step from the one whose execution steps show the press onward, i.e. from step #2 to the end of the episode. The press is shown by EITHER of two signs: the button labelled pressed down, OR the gripper at the button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at a height near 0.03 with fingers closed (0-2% open); the highlighted areas vanishing afterwards confirms it. Either sign alone is the press. Never reverts to `no`. e.g. yes

fields.name: pending_cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] of cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up; the FIRST entry is the next cube to pick. At the first decision step (memory carried in empty, no execution steps) write `[]` explicitly; never leave it blank. When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions (they appear right after the button press and vanish before the decision step), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, and order the entries by where those cubes stand in the object listing of that same execution step: the cube listed earlier among the observed objects comes first (colour groups in the order the listing gives them, e.g. blue before green before red; within one colour the instance listed earlier first). Do NOT order by the order the highlighted areas are listed, by distance to the gripper, by x or by y. Otherwise copy the list carried in, but if the execution steps shown at this step show a pick-up (the gripper descends onto a cube with open fingers, closes to about 46%, and that cube is then marked 'is held in the gripper'), remove the ONE entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest the position where the gripper closed (the held cube's position just before it was lifted), whatever its place in the list, and keep all other entries in their existing order. Do not remove anything on a placing step, i.e. one whose first execution frame already shows a cube held and whose later frames show the fingers opening to ~88-100% and the cube resting on the table again: copy the list unchanged. Never remove an entry just because no cube is currently observed at its position; a cube can be hidden by the arm and still remain pending. Example: highlighted areas at [57, 102] and [110, 105], the listing names the blue cube at [106, 104] before the green cube at [53, 101] -> write [[106, 104], [53, 101]]. Example: carried [[118, 147], [70, 152]], execution steps show the gripper closing at [118, 147] and a cube held -> write [[70, 152]]. e.g. [[106, 104], [53, 101]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of cubes that sit on highlighted white areas and have not yet been picked up; the FIRST entry is always the next cube to pick. `[]` at step #1, written explicitly, never left blank. At the step whose execution steps show the highlighted areas (the button-press step, #2), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube whose position is nearest that area, ordered by where those cubes stand in the observation's object listing at that step (the cube listed earlier among the observed objects comes first; colour groups in the order the listing gives them, and within one colour the instance listed earlier first). Do not order by the order the highlighted areas are listed, by distance to the gripper, by x or by y. At each later step, drop the one entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest the cube that the execution steps show being picked up (gripper descends onto it with open fingers, closes, and the cube is then marked held), whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry in its existing order; the list shrinks by one at each pick-up step. A place step (first execution frame already shows the cube held, later frames show the fingers reopening and the cube resting on the table) leaves the list unchanged. An entry stays in the list even when its cube is not currently among the observed objects (it can be hidden by the arm); only a pick-up drops it. e.g. [[106, 104], [53, 101]] when the blue cube at [106, 104] is listed before the green cube at [53, 101] and both sit on highlighted areas.

initial.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button). Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. If button_pressed is `no` (or memory is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down: choose A, press button. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes, using the current position of the cube seen there in the scene (cube positions wobble; use the cube visible nearest the stored point). 4. If pending_cubes is empty, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose B pointing at the cube nearest the gripper is not needed—instead repeat C (place) as a harmless no-op. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

history.critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Two things were wrong with how this list is filled. First, its order: the recorded pick order does not follow the order in which the highlighted areas are listed (in one episode the area listed second was picked first; in another the three areas were picked first, third, second). The order that best matches the recorded episodes is by x descending, i.e. the cube farthest to the robot's LEFT (largest x) first, then the next-largest x, and so on. So at the button-press step (the step whose execution steps list the highlighted areas), write one entry per highlighted area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, sorted by x from largest to smallest. Second, which entry is dropped: not the first entry, but the entry nearest to the cube that the execution steps show being picked up (gripper descends onto it, it is then marked 'is held in the gripper'). Drop it at the pick-up step only; a step that starts with the cube already held and ends with it released on the table (the place step) leaves the list unchanged. The list must keep an entry even when that cube is no longer listed among observed objects (it can be hidden by the arm); it is dropped only by a pick-up. Example: [[118, 147], [70, 152]] after the button step; [[70, 152]] after the first pick-up; still [[70, 152]] after the place.

field button_pressed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  At the first decision step (memory carried in empty, nothing yet executed) the field is written explicitly as `no`, not left blank; likewise pending_cubes is written explicitly as `[]` there. Every field gets an explicit starting value at the first step.

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT

Ordering: when the execution steps in front of you list highlighted areas, write one entry per area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest each area, and sort the entries by x from largest to smallest (robot's leftmost cube first). Removal: when the execution steps show a pick-up, i.e. the gripper descends to a cube with open fingers, closes to about 46%, and that cube is then marked 'is held in the gripper', remove the ONE entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest to the position where the gripper closed (or to that held cube's position just before it was lifted), whatever its place in the list; keep all other entries. Do not remove anything on a step whose first execution frame already shows a cube held and whose later frames show the fingers opening to ~88-100% and the cube resting on the table again (that is a placing step; copy the list unchanged). Never remove an entry just because no cube is currently observed at its position; cubes can be hidden by the arm and still remain pending. Example: carried [[118, 147], [70, 152]], execution steps show the gripper closing at [118, 147] and a blue cube held -> write [[70, 152]].

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Rule 3 sent the policy wrong by pointing at the first entry of a list that was not in pick order; with the list now sorted by x descending (robot's leftmost first) rule 3 should read: when the gripper is empty, the button has been pressed (memory says yes, or this step's execution steps showed it pressed down) and pending_cubes after this step's update is non-empty, choose B pointing at the first entry of pending_cubes. Add to rule 3: point at that stored [y, x] (or the cube visible within a few pixels of it); if no cube is currently listed at that position it is merely hidden by the arm, still choose B at the stored point, never skip to a later entry and never treat the list as empty. Rule 2 stays: a cube marked held in the scene at the decision step means C. Rule 4 should be rewritten as: only when pending_cubes carried in was already empty and nothing was picked up this step is the task finished, and then C is the harmless no-op; a step that merely shows a placing (fingers reopened, cube back on the table) with a non-empty carried list goes to rule 3, i.e. B at the first carried entry. Rule 5's catch-all can stay but must say the same thing: cube held -> C; any pending entry -> B at its first entry; else A. Also state plainly that the first decision step, with empty memory and no execution steps, is always A.

refused
  One step proposed that the pick order be 'farthest forward (largest y) first'. Across the minibatch that ordering contradicts two other episodes, where a cube with smaller y was picked first; the recorded order is not consistent with largest-y-first, with the listing order of the highlighted areas, nor with nearest-to-gripper. Largest-x-first fits two of the three multi-cube episodes and is what is passed on; the one remaining mismatch (two cubes only five pixels apart in x) cannot be resolved by any ordering visible at the button step, so it is accepted as a residual rather than adding an ad hoc clause. One step proposed removing an entry when the cube 'is no longer on a highlighted area'; highlighted areas vanish before the first pick, so that condition is never observable and is dropped.

history.critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Situation: at the step whose execution steps show the highlighted white areas, the list was filled and sorted by x largest-first, and the subgoal instruction told the policy to pick the first entry. In two episodes the recorded first pick was the last entry, and in a third it was the middle entry; the sort order never matched the pick order, so the list ordering carried no usable fact (SUFFICIENCY failed at the pick steps because the order encoded in the list contradicted the recorded choice). Change: pending_cubes becomes an UNORDERED set written as a list, holding the [y, x] of every cube that sits on a highlighted area and has not yet been picked up. It is `[]` at the first step, filled at the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas (one entry per area: the cube nearest that area, in any order, e.g. the order the areas were listed), and loses the single entry nearest the position where the gripper closed on a cube at each pick-up step; a placing step leaves it unchanged; an entry is never dropped because its cube is momentarily hidden. The selection among the entries is made by the subgoal rule at decision time from the gripper position, not from list order. e.g. [[59, 144], [62, 163], [76, 126]]

Change: button_pressed becomes `yes` from the step whose execution steps show EITHER the button labelled pressed down OR the gripper at the button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at a height near 0.03 with fingers closed (0-2% open); both signs mean the press. the policy prompt for subgoal
  Two rules sent the policy wrong. First, rule 1 conditioned on an execution step literally saying the button is pressed down and on the carried memory; in one episode no step carried that label and the carried memory still said `no`, so the policy chose A again after the press had already happened (SUFFICIENCY). Rule 1 should read: choose A only when the button_pressed value written at THIS step is `no`, i.e. the carried memory says `no` or is empty AND no execution step shown here shows either the pressed-down label or the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers. Every other rule must likewise use the button_pressed and pending_cubes values written at this step, not the carried ones. Second, rule 3 told the policy to point at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes (largest x); the recorded picks were the last entry in two episodes and a middle entry in another, so list position does not choose the cube (SUFFICIENCY). Rule 3 should instead say: when the gripper is empty, button_pressed is `yes` and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty, choose B pointing at the pending entry that is FARTHEST from the gripper's [y, x] at this decision step (largest straight-line distance in image pixels), or at the cube visible within a few pixels of that entry; if that entry's cube is hidden by the arm still point at the stored [y, x]. This farthest-from-gripper choice matched every multi-cube decision in two of the three multi-cube episodes shown. Rules 2, 4 and 5 stay, with rule 5's fallback also pointing at the farthest pending entry rather than the first.

refused
  One multi-cube episode is not covered by the farthest-from-gripper rule: there the recorded picks were, at each decision, the pending cube nearest the gripper (and also in increasing x). The other two multi-cube episodes contradict both 'nearest' and 'smallest x first', and no ordering by x, by y, by distance from the button, by listing order of the highlighted areas, or by colour fits all three; the true pick order appears to be a hidden spawn order that nothing shown reveals. Several steps proposed 'smallest x / robot's rightmost first', 'largest y first' or 'the last entry of the list'; these each fit only the single step that reported them and fail elsewhere, so they are not passed on. The farthest-from-gripper rule is passed on as the criterion that fits the most decisions, with that one episode knowingly left unexplained.

history.critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  The field must become an ORDERED list, not an unordered set, because the order is what settles which cube is picked next. Situation: after the button press the gripper hovers raised with two cubes sitting on highlighted areas; the recorded pick-up is sometimes the cube nearer the gripper and with the smaller y, and sometimes the farther one with the larger y, so neither distance nor position decides it. What decides it across the episodes is the order the cubes appear in the observation listing: objects are listed by colour name (blue, green, red, ...) and within one colour in the order given, and the recorded first pick is always the pending cube that comes earliest in that listing; the second pick is the remaining one. The failure is SUFFICIENCY, with the memory giving the policy no ordering to read. Change: `[]` at the first step as before. At the step whose execution steps show the highlighted areas, write one entry per highlighted area, holding the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, but ORDER the entries by where those cubes stand in the observation listing of that step (earlier-listed colour first; within a colour, the earlier-listed instance first), not by the order the highlighted areas are listed. At every later step, as before, drop the one entry nearest the cube the execution steps show being picked up and keep the others in their existing order; a placing step leaves the list unchanged; an entry stays even while its cube is hidden by the arm. The first entry is always the next cube to pick. e.g. [[106, 104], [53, 101]] when the blue cube at [106, 104] and the green cube at [53, 101] both sit on highlighted areas (blue is listed before green).

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT

When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions, write one entry per highlighted area holding the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, and order the entries by the position of those cubes in the observation listing of the same execution step: the cube whose colour is listed earlier (blue before green before red, i.e. the order the observation uses) comes first, and within one colour the instance listed earlier comes first. Do NOT order by the highlighted-area order, by distance to the gripper, or by y. Otherwise copy the carried list in its existing order, and if the execution steps show a pick-up (gripper descends onto a cube with open fingers, closes to about 46%, the cube is then marked held) remove the one entry nearest the position where the gripper closed, keeping the rest in order. At each later step, drop the one entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest the cube that the execution steps show being picked up (gripper descends onto it with open fingers, closes, and the cube is then marked held), whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry; the list shrinks by one at each pick-up step. A place step (first execution frame already shows the cube held, later frames show the fingers reopening and the cube resting on the table) leaves the list unchanged. An entry stays in the list even when its cube is not currently among the observed objects (it can be hidden by the arm); only a pick-up drops it. e.g. [[89, 146], [63, 150]]

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The episode starts in A (press button): the first decision step, with empty memory and no execution steps, is always A. Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. Choose A, press button, only when the button_pressed value you write at THIS step is `no`: that is, the memory carried in says `no` or is empty AND no execution step shown here shows the press (neither the pressed-down label nor the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers). Every rule below likewise uses the button_pressed and pending_cubes values written at this step, not the carried ones. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes as written at this step (the list is ordered by the cubes' position in the observation listing at the button-press step, and the first entry is always the next cube to pick); never choose by distance from the gripper, by x or by y. Point at that stored [y, x], or at the cube visible within a few pixels of it (cube positions wobble). If no cube is currently listed at that position it is merely hidden by the arm: still choose B at the stored point; never switch to another entry for that reason and never treat the list as empty. 4. Only when the pending_cubes carried in was already empty, nothing was picked up at this step, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op. A step that merely shows a placing (fingers reopened, cube back on the table) with a non-empty carried list is not finished: apply rule 3 and choose B at the first entry of pending_cubes. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Write `no` when the memory carried in says `no` (or is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the press (neither the pressed-down label nor the gripper at the button's position at low height with closed fingers). At the first decision step, when the memory carried in is empty, write the starting value `no` explicitly; never leave the field blank. Write `yes` as soon as any execution step shown at this step either says the button is pressed down, or shows the gripper within a few pixels of the button's [y, x] at a height of about 0.02-0.04 with fingers nearly closed (0-2% open); the highlighted areas then vanish from the listing before the decision step, which confirms the press. Either sign alone is enough; do not wait for the label. Write `yes` also whenever the memory carried in already says `yes`. Never go back to `no`. e.g. yes
fields.annotation: `no` at step #1 (nothing has happened yet), written explicitly, never left blank. `yes` at every step from the one whose execution steps show the press onward, i.e. from step #2 to the end of the episode. The press is shown by EITHER of two signs: the button labelled pressed down, OR the gripper at the button's [y, x] (within a few pixels) at a height near 0.03 with fingers closed (0-2% open); the highlighted areas vanishing afterwards confirms it. Either sign alone is the press. Never reverts to `no`. e.g. yes

fields.name: pending_cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] of cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up; the FIRST entry is the next cube to pick. At the first decision step (memory carried in empty, no execution steps) write `[]` explicitly; never leave it blank. When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions (they appear right after the button press and vanish before the decision step), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, and order the entries by where those cubes stand in the object listing of that same execution step: the cube listed earlier among the observed objects comes first (colour groups in the order the listing gives them, e.g. blue before green before red; within one colour the instance listed earlier first). Do NOT order by the order the highlighted areas are listed, by distance to the gripper, by x or by y. Otherwise copy the list carried in, but if the execution steps shown at this step show a pick-up (the gripper descends onto a cube with open fingers, closes to about 46%, and that cube is then marked 'is held in the gripper'), remove the ONE entry whose stored [y, x] is nearest the position where the gripper closed (the held cube's position just before it was lifted), whatever its place in the list, and keep all other entries in their existing order. Do not remove anything on a placing step, i.e. one whose first execution frame already shows a cube held and whose later frames show the fingers opening to ~88-100% and the cube resting on the table again: copy the list unchanged. Never remove an entry just because no cube is currently observed at its position; a cube can be hidden by the arm and still remain pending. Example: highlighted areas at [57, 102] and [110, 105], the listing names the blue cube at [106, 104] before the green cube at [53, 101] -> write [[106, 104], [53, 101]]. Example: carried [[118, 147], [70, 152]], execution steps show the gripper closing at [118, 147] and a cube held -> write [[70, 152]]. e.g. [[106, 104], [53, 101]]
